subject: Redwood readiness: latency & warm-pool checkpoints for peak window
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Katie Rose <katie@brightside.com>, Brightside Engineering <ops@brightside.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Jan 2028 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Redwood readiness: latency & warm-pool checkpoints for peak window

Hi Katie / Brightside team —

Thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap of the performance commitments you asked us to validate and the concrete next steps so we stay aligned for the Nov 2028 holiday peak: 

Key SLOs you mentioned (from discovery):
- Short interactive responses (<= 128 tokens): p95 latency target 220ms end-to-end (API entry to first token).
- Streaming long responses (>=512 tokens): per-token delta latency <= 50ms and average token throughput target 5.5k tokens/sec across the fleet.
- Concurrency: sustained concurrent sessions up to 600 (peak bursts to 1,000 for <10 minutes).
- Graceful degradation: fallback to smaller model variant within 3s for requests approaching timeout window.

Autoscaling / burst specifics we discussed:
- Warm pool: recommend initial warm pool of 35–45 prewarmed instances (same model/quantization as prod) to hit p95 target for cold-to-hot latency during sudden surges.
- Scale-up times: target cold-start-to-ready under 90s for new GPUs; warm-pool activation <5s for prewarmed instances.
- Queueing behavior: soft queueing on excess requests with per-account priority (premium lanes can preempt standard lanes). Queue TTL 12s before triggering fallback model route.

Action items and owners:
1) Brightside: share 48h traffic sample (representative peak + baseline) — Emma / Katie (you mentioned you could export a replayable JSON). (due: Jan 20)
2) Redwood (Monica / Marcus): run replay tests against a staging cluster that mirrors the intended model variant and provide SLO heatmaps (latency percentiles, token throughput, scale-up timeline). Draft perf test plan attached. (target start: Jan 23)
3) Redwood (Ben): provide proposal with estimated committed warm-pool sizing, cost delta for reserved warm capacity, and recommended fallback routing policy. (draft by Jan 25)
4) Schedule canary run in Brightside staging with 1-hour simulated peak once replay results are validated — coordinate calendar after results.

Attachments: redwood_perf_test_plan.xlsx (test cases + measurement hooks).

Questions for you now:
- Does Brightside require a hard upper bound on acceptable queue TTL (you mentioned 15s previously — we proposed 12s)?
- Any constraint on model fallback behavior (e.g., prefer smaller but same-family model, or always prefer non-streaming shorter outputs)?

I'll follow up with Monica to kick off the replay once we get the sample.

— Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1-415-555-0182

From: Katie Rose <katie@brightside.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Brightside Engineering <ops@brightside.com>, Emma Lopez <emma@purchasing.brightside.com>
Date: Fri, 19 Jan 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Redwood readiness: latency & warm-pool checkpoints for peak window

Thanks Ben — that recap looks correct and appreciated. Quick clarifications from our side: 

- Queue TTL: we want to keep user-facing waits under 12s where possible. If a fallback is triggered after TTL, the user flow should still return a result (smaller model or cached response).
- Fallback model: prefer same-family smaller variant (we care about semantic consistency more than exact token matching).
- Data residency: staging tests must run in us-west region to match our compliance constraints.
- Cost: can you provide a delta estimate for maintaining a 40-instance warm pool vs. a reactive-only strategy? We'll need that for procurement.

I've attached a 48h sample (brightside_traffic_sample.json) — it's scrubbed but includes timestamps, session ids, and token-length distributions. We'll also need an NDA/contract draft for reserved capacity. Emma is on copy to coordinate purchase approvals.

Thanks — Katie
Katie Rose
Head of Product 
Brightside Retail
katie@brightside.com

Subject: Re: Redwood readiness: latency & warm-pool checkpoints for peak window

Katie / Emma —

Received the traffic sample, thanks. Monica and Marcus: can you confirm test schedule availability next week? Proposed test plan (high level):

1) Replay the 48h sample into a staging cluster in us-west that mirrors Brightside's intended model variant and quantization. Measure: p50/p90/p95 latency, per-token streaming delta, token throughput, and instance activation time series.
2) Controlled burst tests: ramp to 1,000 concurrent sessions with a synthetic mix for 15-minute peak windows to validate warm-pool sizing and queue TTL behavior.
3) Canary fallback simulation: induce TTL expirations and validate fallback routing (smaller variant) and end-to-end behavioral differences.

Deliverables: test result report (CSV+charts), suggested warm-pool sizing with confidence bounds, recommended queue TTL and fallback thresholds, and a one-page cost delta estimate for warm pool vs reactive. We'll attach perf artifacts to the HubSpot deal and drive a short readout.

Monica — can you also include a config snippet for the warm-pool activation policy (how we prewarm, how we mark healthy instances for immediate routing)? Marcus — please validate the streaming per-token measurement hooks so we get consistent deltas.

Proposed timeline: start replay Jan 24, controlled burst Jan 25 (if replay results ok), readout Jan 26; Ben to send draft commercial with warm-pool cost delta Jan 25.

Link to test plan and trackers: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1A2b3C-redwood-brightside-testplan
Attachments: redwood_perf_test_plan.xlsx (updated)

— Ben

Ben — will take point on the replay and the benchmarking. Quick notes from planning: 

- We'll run everything in us-west to match compliance.
- Initial warm-pool candidate sizing: start at 40 instances and iterate down/up based on observed cold-hit rate and queuing during the controlled burst. We'll produce a confidence-band (40 +/- 8) after replay.
- Measurement hooks: we'll capture token-level timestamps at the model entry and model emit points for streaming delta, and aggregate at 1s windows for token throughput.
- Scale timing: we'll instrument instance activation (boot -> health-check -> ready) and warming handoff. Expect median warm activation ~65s on our config; warm-pool activation for prewarmed instances should be <3s.

Deliverables we'll upload to the Drive link and HubSpot:
- perf-results-raw.csv
- perf-heatmap.png
- warm-pool-sizing-recommendation.pdf
- configuration-snippet.txt (warm pool activation policy)

Schedule: replay starts Jan 24 (as Ben set), controlled burst Jan 25; readout Jan 26 morning — I'll post a calendar invite.

— Monica
